lessons.story:
Five words guide Jo's review: boundary, subtract, durations, active, and surplus. She writes a number beside each word and then explains what that number represents. Her teacher says the explanation matters more than producing a long list of correct-looking figures.

For the volunteer message, four o'clock is a boundary on available help, not a new starting time. For the toy car, Jo must subtract the starting timer reading from the finishing reading to compare durations. A final display of thirteen does not mean thirteen seconds of travel.

In the reading challenge, thirty minutes inside a library may contain fewer active reading minutes. Jo removes breaks before checking the daily target. She also keeps surplus minutes on their actual day rather than moving them to another. The review helps her see that arithmetic works only after she identifies the quantity, its limits, and the rule under which it is being counted.
lessons.title: A Number Needs Its Definition
